findings.F1: Sense 1 definition says uncountable noun / not much instead of plural countable noun / not many.
findings.F2: Sense 2 example 'Could I borrow a few money?' is ungrammatical.
findings.F3: Usage note gives less/least as the comparative and superlative of few instead of fewer/fewest.
findings.F4: The few versus a few contrast is stated repeatedly across fields, including twice within sense 2's explanation.
findings.F5: The plural-countable-only rule (little for uncountable nouns) is restated in the adaptation grammar note and the learner-error note.
findings.F6: Inflections omit the real forms fewer and fewest.
findings.F7: 'every few' (every few minutes, every few weeks) is not covered.
findings.F8: 'quite a few' (meaning a fairly large number) has no phrase definition.
